hero.heading: Johns Dental Laboratories, a cost model sent for correction
hero.caption: Built October 3, 2026, from johnsdental.com, including the history, products, and resources pages, and from public metal prices. No federal index is used, and this page says why. Every number is labeled; the assumptions are sliders; move them and the number moves.
hero.liveCaption: The model's estimate, on the assumptions you have set below
hero.subline: (exact: $43,145 and $366,700), each rounded to the nearest $5,000 for display; the exact figures govern.

model.heading: Move our assumptions
model.intro: Each slider is one of the assumptions in our letter, set to the range we wrote down. If you know a figure, narrow its range, or close both handles on the exact number. The estimate above then follows your figures instead of ours. Tap a figure to type it exactly.

volume.label: Units you ship in a year
volume.caption: Optional. Type your volume and every dollar figure on this page scales to your year. Leave it empty and the model stays per ten thousand units.

sliders.label: Units replaced under your replacement program
sliders.basis: Against a national remake average near 4 percent, per trade sources [[BENCHMARK]]. Assumed, printed to be corrected [[ASSUMED]].

sliders.label: Fully loaded cost of one replacement
Consultation hours per ten thousand units
sliders.basis: 500 to 2,000 hours is 3 to 12 minutes a unit, on the phone or at the bench, before a case ships. Assumed, printed to be corrected [[ASSUMED]].

sliders.label: Loaded cost of one technician hour
Share of units that carry precious metal
sliders.basis: Full cast and porcelain fused to metal; chrome cobalt, wire, and zirconia carry no drift. Assumed, printed to be corrected [[ASSUMED]].

sliders.label: Precious metal value in one unit

constants.text: Metal uses the public gold price, $4,177 on October 1, 2026 against $3,864 a year earlier (+8.1 percent) [[BENCHMARK]], applied only to units that carry precious metal. Chrome cobalt, wire, and zirconia have no public curve and are charged nothing.

model.disclosure: This model carries no federal index: none maps onto a dental laboratory.

terms.label: Metal drift on units that carry precious metal

model.formulaText: Moved per 10,000 units = 10,000 × replacement share × replacement cost + consultation hours × hourly rate + 10,000 × precious metal share × metal value × 0.081
model.plainText: In words, the replacements your program absorbs at their full cost, plus the consultation hours that ship at a price of zero, plus the slice of this year's gold rise carried by the units that hold precious metal.
model.callout: What nobody prices is that consultation. Sixty appliances means a dentist choosing one calls first, and the call ships at a price of zero. Nobody counts the minutes per case, which appliances generate the calls, or how often a replacement under your own program began as a question nobody asked. A family laboratory's answer is its people, if what they know is written down for the doctor. Nobody has written it down.

respect.heading: What you already show in the open
paragraphs: Your family opened a denture laboratory in Terre Haute in 1939; you took the responsibility as the third generation and kept it family run across four departments [[OBSERVED]].
Your own history page says you were among the first to take up all-ceramic crowns, acetyl-resin clasping, and chair-side scanning [[OBSERVED]].
A catalog of some sixty named orthodontic appliances. A turn-time calculator any doctor can run. A replacement program and a customer service guarantee, both in writing [[OBSERVED]].
A promise most laboratories would not print: technicians always on hand to answer questions and provide consultation [[OBSERVED]].

proposal.heading: What we propose
proposal.lead: The proposal: the count (consultation minutes and replacements by appliance), the appliance book (one page per family, in your technicians' words), and the thirty-day result; fixed fee between $1,200 and $1,800; read-only; no patient information leaves the building.

ledger.title: What a page of the consultation log looks like
ledger.label: Illustrative, not Johns Dental Laboratories data
ledger.note: Priced at $72 an hour. Four of five calls ask what one page of the book could answer; the fifth needs a technician's judgment. Every call and figure is invented to show the format.

proposal.promise: If your records show our printed range overstated your exposure, our findings letter says so in those words.
